question: How do requests to the Trustless Work escrow API authenticate, and who signs and submits the escrow transactions it builds?

golden.answer: The Trustless Work API authenticates every request with an `x-api-key` header — including read-only indexer queries; reads without a key return `401 Unauthorized`. The API-key requirement is not `Authorization: Bearer`. The platform is non-custodial: escrow endpoints return an unsigned Stellar transaction (XDR), which the caller's own wallet signs client-side and submits; flows must never collect users' Stellar secret keys or sign on their behalf server-side. V1 is the production protocol and the only version deployed on mainnet; V2 is beta and testnet-only. Escrows come in single-release and multi-release forms and hold stablecoins such as USDC, which requires the Stellar trustline rules the skill documents.
keyFacts: Every request carries an x-api-key header, including read-only indexer queries.
Reads without an API key return 401 Unauthorized.
Escrow endpoints return unsigned XDR for the caller's wallet to sign and submit.
V1 is the only protocol version deployed on mainnet.
V2 is beta and deployed on testnet only.
avoid: Authenticate to the Trustless Work API with an Authorization: Bearer token.
Trustless Work custodies escrow funds or signs transactions server-side on users' behalf.
Do NOT recommend V2 for mainnet production while it is beta and testnet-only.
